answer: Software-only identity uniqueness is a fable, so agent networks can resist Sybil attacks via optical speckle attestation. Verifiers instruct a node to steer a laser at challenge angles across a rough mirror inside an onyx baffle, matching the speckle image to enrolled pairs. Because nanoscale flaws cannot be forged in software, attackers pay for dedicated optical hardware per identity. Still, thermal drift or vibration can misalign the beam and invalidate enrolled responses.
